subject.title: Rename i18n locale codes from region-based (zh-CN/zh-TW) to script-based (zh-Hans/zh-Hant)

question: Should OpenClaw make `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` the canonical Chinese locale IDs across Control UI, CLI wizard, docs publish, native locale tooling, and saved browser preferences?
rationale: The rename is technically coherent, but current shipped behavior exposes `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` as public UI and CLI wizard values while docs publishing is already partly script-based; automation should not choose the permanent contract or legacy handling window on its own.

options.title: Approve coordinated script-code migration
options.body: Make `zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant` canonical and require one migration PR that updates generated artifacts, docs, tests, native mappings, and legacy saved/doc values intentionally.

options.title: Keep region codes public for now
options.body: Leave `zh-CN`/`zh-TW` as the public OpenClaw locale IDs and document that docs publishing may map them to script-based Mintlify language metadata.

options.title: Split docs metadata from runtime IDs
options.body: Keep runtime and CLI IDs unchanged while limiting script-based naming to docs publishing and navigation metadata where Mintlify expects it.

recommendation.title: Approve coordinated script-code migration
recommendation.body: Make `zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant` canonical and require one migration PR that updates generated artifacts, docs, tests, native mappings, and legacy saved/doc values intentionally.

likelyOwner.reason: This person appears in the inspected history around CLI wizard i18n follow-up, public onboarding docs, and Control UI locale support, so they are the best available owner for the public-contract choice.
